answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before earning trust. Creating thousands of fake accounts then costs real capital per identity, like a comet that burns up most of its mass on entry: cheap to launch one, ruinous to launch ten thousand. The vault releases the stake only after a long, clean work history, so a fraudster's plume of sock-puppets must each survive months of honest behavior before paying off. The bond is slashed on proven abuse, turning identity forgery from a free trick into a priced, losing trade.
